rounds.text: The market severely under-appreciates Compucom Software Ltd by pricing the stock at a steep discount to its underlying net asset value, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.75x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.3x [E2, E7]. This asset-backed safety is further highlighted by the stock sitting deeply depressed at only 18% of its 52-week range, offering an entry point well below its intrinsic book value of ₹ 17.9 per share against a market price of ₹ 13.5 [E2, E5]. Far from a stagnant asset, the business is demonstrating clear operational momentum with profit growth exceeding 20% year-on-year alongside accelerating earnings growth [E70, E72]. This fundamental turnaround is supported by a solid 5-year compounded sales growth rate of 14% [E15], outpacing the broader economy's historical baseline. Furthermore, investors are paid to wait with a positive dividend yield of 1.47% [E4] while the company capitalizes on favorable sector tailwinds that feature a median sales growth of 12.9% [E82]. Conceded: [E14], [E16], [E26], [E27], [E28], [E29], [E73], [E74].

The company trades at an extreme trailing price-to-earnings multiple of 162x according to filed statements, while a secondary metric places the P/E at 36.51x against a sector benchmark of just 26.5x [E1, E6]. This premium valuation is completely disconnected from its underlying profitability, evidenced by a dismal 10-year median return on equity of 3% that deteriorates further to a 0% median ROE over the last year [E26, E29]. Long-term top-line erosion compounds these concerns, with compounded sales growth contracting at -6% over 10 years and plunging by -17% over 3 years [E14, E16]. Operational returns lag drastically behind industry peers, as demonstrated by a meager ROCE of 1.9% compared to a sector median of 8.4% [E12, E83]. Furthermore, speculative enthusiasm has clearly outpaced operational reality, with recent price growth exceeding profit growth by 32% while the stock languishes at just 18% of its 52-week range [E5, E58]. Conceded: the company displays a low price-to-book ratio of 0.75x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.3x alongside recent YoY profit growth exceeding 20% [E2, E7, E70].

The bear relies heavily on the trailing P/E of 162x [E1], yet ignores that the stock trades at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.75x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.3x [E7], meaning assets are acquired well below their stated value [E2]. While the bear points to low historical ROE figures [E26, E29], it overlooks clear proof of operational momentum, specifically that earnings growth is accelerating alongside profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E70, E72]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years is -17% [E16] and ROCE stands at a low 1.9% [E12]. However, the bear's claim of long-term top-line erosion [E14, E16] is contradicted by a strong 14% compounded sales growth rate over a 5-year horizon [E15]. Finally, the assertion that the stock is driven purely by speculative enthusiasm [E58] is undermined by the fact that the equity sits near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 18% of its span [E5].

Conceded: the stock trades at 0.75x book value [E2]. However, the bull's reliance on this P/B discount as a margin of safety ignores that low asset pricing is a direct byproduct of chronically depressed capital productivity, specifically a dismal 10-year median ROE of 3% [E26] that recently hit 0% [E29]. The bull points to accelerating earnings growth [E72], but this short-term blip cannot mask a structural top-line contraction where 3-year compounded sales growth plummeted by -17% [E16] and 10-year growth sits at -6% [E14], severely underperforming the sector median sales growth of 12.9% [E82]. Finally, the bull cites a sector benchmark for P/B [E7], yet completely glosses over the fact that the company's own ROCE of 1.9% [E12] and last year's ROE of 0% [E29] are fractionates of the sector median ROCE of 8.4% [E83].
